messages.author: e5c7e56038437512
messages.subject: variable factor with autocorrelation or "rw1"
parts:
Hello everyone!

I have a question related with a model spatio-temporal.
Can I specify "rw1" or "ar1" in temporal effect for a variable that I declared how "factor"?
I want obtain the coefficients for each "year" in different types of models proposed.

I hope you can help me
Regards!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] variable factor with autocorrelation or "rw1"
parts:
Hi,

I'm not sure if I understand the question. could you give a simple
example?

a comment: factors are not ordered, and using them as input into an
ordered model like ar1, will not make sense. then its easier to
convert the factor into integers, say.


H

Hi 

Thanks for you help

Thanks for your help
For example, in a GLM, if I want the coefficient of the variable "year" (just how example) i declared a "year" how factor.

In INLA, if I want a coefficient  for the variable "year" How should I declare into of linear predictor?

My data.stack is:

stk.dat <- inla.stack(data=list(y=dat$REND),   
            A=list(A,1), tag="est",              
            effects=list(list(i=1:spde$n.spde),   
            data.frame(Intercept=1,               
            year=inla.group(dat$year),
            ship=inla.group(dat$ship)))) 

Formula:
formula   <- y ~ 0 + Intercept + f(i, model=spde) + f(ship, model="rw1") + f(year, model="iid")

Regards

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] variable factor with autocorrelation or "rw1"
parts:
Honestly, I have always used simplified laplace, because that option comes highly recommended (it is also the default option).

You can change it to laplace and check if there is any difference. But you will have to run both models.

To see the difference, compare the linear predictor or the fitted value posteriors, plot for example 0.05, 0.5 and 0.95 quantiles. These should match quite well, but not perfectly, on top of each other (for the two models).

Kind regards,
Haakon
